prompt: A bank with five thousand engineers and Carreto with fifty both do enterprise architecture. What differs, by the lesson?

choices.text: Carreto is too small to need any
choices.why: The lesson says Carreto needs a small amount, and Renata builds it.

choices.text: The effort: a department there, a page and a spreadsheet here
choices.why: Right: the questions are the same; the amount of machinery is not.

choices.text: The bank's version looks at years, Carreto's at weeks
choices.why: Both judge enterprise decisions years out.

choices.text: Only the bank maps capabilities to systems
choices.why: Carreto's map was the first thing Renata built at this level.

prompt: What is the horizon of solution architecture?

choices.text: A single sprint
choices.why: One sprint builds a part; the solution's contracts outlive the build.

choices.text: Three to five years
choices.why: That is the enterprise horizon.

choices.text: Months of building, then years running
choices.why: Right: built in weeks or months, and its contracts outlive the code written then.

choices.text: The life of one major version of a service
choices.why: That describes an application decision's horizon.

prompt: The Tracking team wants to split its own database into a table per month to keep queries fast. Nothing it exposes to other systems changes. Which level is that?

choices.text: Application: it stays inside one system
choices.why: Right: the first question passes, so the team decides.

choices.text: Solution, because positions feed the 24-hour payout
choices.why: The payout relies on Tracking's contract, which does not change here.

choices.text: Enterprise, because databases are a company-wide concern
choices.why: One team's internal storage is not a shared platform.

choices.text: It needs Renata's approval before it counts as any level
choices.why: Placing a decision does not depend on who approves it.

prompt: The Shipper team calls Pricing for every quote it shows. What does it need to know about Pricing's architecture?
hint: Lesson 4: the audience of application architecture.

choices.text: The two stages of the quote calculation
choices.why: Those are internals; a caller has no use for them.

choices.text: Which routing provider sits behind the adapter
choices.why: The adapter exists so callers need not know.

choices.text: The full component diagram of the service
choices.why: That is for the team that builds Pricing.

choices.text: The contract and how Pricing behaves when it fails
choices.why: Right: callers need the agreed time or an explicit error, and nothing else.

prompt: Match each level to its time horizon.
Why does the lesson say solution architecture is where a company of Carreto's size most needs its first architect?
hint: Lesson 4: who was doing each level before Renata?

choices.text: Because enterprise frameworks are too expensive to adopt
choices.why: Cost of frameworks is not the argument.

choices.text: Because the teams design their own services badly
choices.why: The lesson says each team designs its own service well.

choices.text: Nobody owned the journeys between teams
choices.why: Right: application work had owners; the work between teams was being done by nobody.

choices.text: Because solution work is the most senior of the three
choices.why: The levels are not ranks.
